title: From a roll of steel to a car
_story: Steve crafts a minecart from iron in one click. Ismaeel follows a real car through a factory: a coil of steel, pressed panels, robots welding with sparks, paint, the assembly line, and a test drive.
_stepChain: crafting vs a factory → steel coil → press shapes panels → robots weld → estimate the welds (about 5,000) → paint layers (rust) → assembly line adds battery, motor, seats, windows, wheels → tap parts → test drive → 4 wheels × 6 cars

talk.ask: What are the main jobs in a car factory?
talk.goodAnswer: pressing steel into shapes, welding them together, painting, then adding all the parts on the assembly line, and testing.

talk.ask: Why do factories use robots for welding?
talk.goodAnswer: robots don't get tired and put every weld in exactly the right place, thousands of times a day; people do the jobs that need careful hands and eyes.

handsOn: Next time you're in a car park, look closely at a car door edge with a grown-up. Can you see where two pieces of metal are joined? Count the wheels on 3 cars.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: In my world, I put 5 iron ingots in the crafting table, and pop! A minecart! But a real car has thousands and thousands of parts. How do people put a car together?
Most of a car's body is made of a strong metal called steel. It comes to the factory as a giant roll of thin steel, as tall as Steve! It's called a coil.
The steel is cut into flat sheets. Then a huge machine called a press squashes each sheet into a shape. Ka-CHUNK! Like pressing play dough into a mould! Doors, a roof, sides, and a bonnet.
Now robots join the pieces together! Zap! They use electricity to melt a tiny spot of metal. It cools, and holds the pieces tight. Each little spot is called a weld.
The robots make weld after weld after weld, all over the car. Zap, zap, zap!

question.prompt: How many welds do you think one car has?
question.reveal: About 5,000 welds in a family car! Every single one in exactly the right place.

narration.text: Steel goes brown and crumbly if it gets wet. That's called rust. Yuck! So the car is painted in layers. First a coat that stops rust. Then the colour! Then a clear, shiny coat on top.
Then the car rolls slowly along a moving track. People and machines add the parts, one by one. The battery, the motor, the seats, the windows, and the wheels! That's called an assembly line.
Tap a part, and find out what it does!

parts.label: Battery
parts.narration: The big flat battery under the floor is like a lunchbox for electricity. It stores it up.

parts.label: Motor
parts.narration: The motor uses the electricity to turn the wheels. Vroom!

parts.label: Wheel
parts.narration: Rubber tyres grip the road, so the car doesn't slide.

parts.label: Body
parts.narration: The strong steel body keeps everyone safe inside.

narration.speaker: steve
narration.text: Last, every car gets tested! The lights: flash! The brakes: screech! And a drive. Off it goes! Vroom!
The factory puts 4 wheels on every car.

0.hint: Every car gets its own 4 wheels. Count 4 at a time.
0.say: You added 6 and 4. Count 4 for each car: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24!

2.say: 20 is only 5 cars. One more car adds 4 more: 24!

rule.text: Press it, weld it, paint it, build it, test it.
rule.ask: How is a car made? Say it out loud! Then tap the eye.
rule.spoken: Steel is pressed into shapes, welded together, painted, then the parts are added on the assembly line, and every car is tested.

bonus.prompt: Bonus! Each car has 4 seats. How many seats in 3 cars?

0.hint: Each car has its own 4 seats.
0.say: You added 3 and 4. Count 4 for each car: 4, 8, 12.

2.say: 8 is 2 cars. The third car adds 4 more: 12.
